newsitem.title: USA: State to repay $1.4 billion to Calpers fund.
newsitem.headline: State to repay $1.4 billion to Calpers fund.

text.p: California will repay the California Public Employees' Retirement System about $1.4 billion for funds the state used to balance its budgets in the early 1990s, state officials said Thursday.

Republican Gov. Pete Wilson had asked the California Supreme Court to overturn the ruling by a state appeals court, which held in February that the state improperly withheld the money from Calpers, the nation's largest public pension fund.

But the state's Supreme Court this week refused to rehear the case and now California must repay Calpers the withheld funds, estimated at $1.36 billion, according to California's Department of Finance.
"This is the end of the legal process," Chris Waddell, chief counsel for the department, said.
The money owed to the pension fund represents nearly 3 percent of the state's proposed $51.7 billion general fund budget for the fiscal year that begins on July 1.
State lawmakers are expected to consider ways to repay the money during their budget deliberations.
"What is not clear is what the timing is for the repayment of the obligation," said Department of Finance spokesman H.D. Palmer. "We are looking into that issue as we speak."
The dispute erupted in 1992 as the state struggled to cope with its deepest economic downturn since the Depression.
As a result of new laws passed by the state legislature in 1992 and 1993, state employer contributions that would have been paid during fiscal 1993 and 1994 were not paid in those years.
In 1994, Calpers sued the governor and other top state officials, arguing that the measures were unconstitutional.
The trial court hearing the case agreed, ruling in 1995 that "in arrears" financing was unconstitutional, and directed the governor to disregard the measures and to reimburse the retirement fund.
The governor appealed and in February, the appeals court affirmed the trial court decision.
The governor appealed again, but the state Supreme Court said it would let the appellate ruling stand.
Calpers welcomed the Supreme Court decision.
"We think this is a sigificant vindication of the Calpers legal position," spokeswoman Patricia Macht said.

Calpers, the nation's largest public pension fund, provides retirement and health benefits to more than 1 million active and retired public employees and their families and manages more than $110 billion in assets.
